## Anthropic / Claude Code

**[1]** "Pricing." *Anthropic*, n.d.
<https://claude.com/pricing>
**Tier:** 2
Pro $20/mo ($17/mo annual, billed $200 up front), Max 5x from $100/mo, Max 20x from $200/mo, Team Standard $20/$25 per seat, Team Premium $100/$125 per seat. Claude Code is included on all paid tiers including Pro. Models listed: Opus, Sonnet, Haiku.

**[2]** "Claude Code overview." *Claude Code Docs*, n.d.
<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview>
**Tier:** 2
Surfaces: Terminal CLI (curl/PowerShell/CMD/Homebrew/WinGet/apt/dnf/apk), VS Code extension, JetBrains plugin (beta), Desktop app (macOS, Windows x64, Windows ARM64), Web (claude.ai/code), iOS app. Third-party providers supported in Terminal CLI and VS Code (Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Microsoft Foundry, Google Vertex AI). Auto memory, hooks, MCP, sub-agents, Routines (cloud-scheduled), Desktop scheduled tasks, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD, Slack, Chrome.

**[3]** "Updates to our Consumer Terms." *Anthropic*, August 28, 2025.
<https://www.anthropic.com/news/updates-to-our-consumer-terms>
**Tier:** 2
Effective Aug 28 2025 (rolling out), with Oct 8 2025 selection deadline. Applies to Free, Pro, Max plans (including when those plans use Claude Code). Excludes Claude for Work, Government, Education, and API via Bedrock/Vertex AI. Users choose to allow training data use; if enabled, retention extends to 5 years (de-identified); if declined, 30-day retention.

**[4]** "How long do you store my data?" *Anthropic Privacy Center*, n.d.
<https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/10023548-how-long-do-you-store-my-data>
**Tier:** 2
Deleted chats removed within 30 days. If model improvement enabled, chats and coding sessions retained up to 5 years de-identified. If disabled, no future training use. Trust & safety violations: inputs/outputs 2 years, classification scores 7 years. Feedback retained 5 years. Incognito chats excluded from training regardless of setting.

**[5]** Willison, Simon. "The Claude Code confusion." *simonwillison.net*, April 22, 2026.
<https://simonwillison.net/2026/apr/22/claude-code-confusion/>
**Tier:** 3
Anthropic silently moved Claude Code from $20 Pro plan to Max-only on April 22 2026 (a "~2% test" per employee tweet), then reverted within hours. No formal announcement. Willison: "A tweet from an employee is not the way to make an announcement like this." Notes OpenAI's Codex remains on free + $20 plans as a safer alternative for educators.

**[6]** "Claude Code Skills, MCP, and Plugins: Comparison Guide." *MorphLLM*, n.d.
<https://www.morphllm.com/claude-code-skills-mcp-plugins>
**Tier:** 3
Skills cost ~30-50 tokens until invoked. MCP servers can consume significant context: a typical 5-server setup with 58 tools uses ~55,000 tokens before any conversation starts. Anthropic's Tool Search reduces this overhead by ~85%. Plugins bundle skills + MCP + hooks + commands + subagents.

## Cursor

**[7]** "Pricing." *Cursor*, n.d.
<https://cursor.com/pricing>
**Tier:** 2
Hobby (free), Pro $20/mo, Pro+ $60/mo (3x usage on OpenAI/Claude/Gemini models), Ultra $200/mo (20x usage), Teams $40/user/mo, Enterprise custom. Pro+ marked "Recommended."

**[8]** "Composer 2 — Cursor's frontier coding model." *Cursor Blog*, March 19, 2026.
<https://cursor.com/blog/composer-2>
**Tier:** 2
Released March 19, 2026. CursorBench: 61.3. Terminal-Bench 2.0: 61.7 (Composer 2 vs Claude Opus 4.6 at 58.0; GPT-5.4 at 75.1). SWE-bench Multilingual: 73.7. Pricing: standard $0.50/M input + $2.50/M output; fast $1.50/M + $7.50/M. Composer 1.5 scored 44.2 on CursorBench; Composer 1 was 38.0. "Fast" is now the default.

**[9]** "Data Use & Privacy Overview." *Cursor*, n.d.
<https://cursor.com/data-use>
**Tier:** 2
Privacy Mode ON: zero data retention with model providers; "None of your code will ever be trained on by us or any third-party." Privacy Mode OFF: Cursor collects codebase data, prompts, editor actions, code snippets — used to train models. Inference providers (Baseten, Together AI, Fireworks) temporarily access data. Embeddings and metadata (file hashes, names) may persist even with Privacy Mode on. Accounts created before Oct 15, 2025 have different sharing restrictions.

**[10]** Zeff, Maxwell. "Cursor apologizes for unclear pricing changes that upset users." *TechCrunch*, July 7, 2025.
<https://techcrunch.com/2025/07/07/cursor-apologizes-for-unclear-pricing-changes-that-upset-users/>
**Tier:** 3
June 16, 2025: Cursor switched Pro plan from "500 fast responses + unlimited slower" to a $20 usage credit billed at API rates. Users on Anthropic Claude models ran out of requests "rather quickly." CEO Michael Truell apology blog post July 4, 2025: "We recognize that we didn't handle this pricing rollout well and we're sorry." Anysphere offered refunds.

**[11]** Massimo et al. "[Critical] Cursor 2.1.50 - Multiple regressions: random sandbox, context loss, file corruption, save failures." *Cursor Forum*, December 2025.
<https://forum.cursor.com/t/critical-cursor-2-1-50-multiple-regressions-random-sandbox-context-loss-file-corruption-save-failures/145648>
**Tier:** 4
Five reported regressions in Cursor 2.1.50: random sandbox terminal mode (network/browser blocked), context loss between sessions, unauthorized file creation, save failures (changes not persisted), file corruption (files emptied during save). Cursor team member Dean Rie acknowledged the network sandbox bug ("bug identified, fix in progress") on Dec 9, 2025. Topic auto-closed Dec 31, 2025. No follow-up resolution details in the thread.

**[17]** "Gemini Code Assist quotas." *Google for Developers*, last updated April 23, 2026.
<https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/resources/quotas>
**Tier:** 2
Individual (free) tier: 1,000 requests per user per day. Standard: 1,500/user/day. Enterprise: 2,000/user/day. Local codebase awareness uses 1,000,000-token context window. **Tier:** 2

Supports Gemini 3 Pro plus Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.5 and OpenAI's GPT-OSS at launch. Manager Surface for spawning/orchestrating multiple agents asynchronously. Editor View, Artifacts, Knowledge Base.

<https://aitoolanalysis.com/google-antigravity-review/>
**Tier:** 3

**Tier:** 2
Individual (free) tier code prompts and answers may be collected and used for model training; opt-out available in settings. Data is disconnected from Google Account before human review and retained up to 18 months in disconnected form. Standard and Enterprise editions do not collect prompts and do not use them for training.

First-run experience: imports existing VS Code settings and extensions, plus Cursor and Windsurf preferences. Resolves the architecture ambiguity in [26].

**[28]** Cleaver, Alex. "Bob 1.0 Users Bugged By Lack Of One Feature." *IT Jungle*, April 6, 2026.
<https://www.itjungle.com/2026/04/06/bob-1-0-users-bugged-by-lack-of-one-feature/>

**[29]** Litten, Nick. "IBM Bob Pricing Explained: Free Trial, Bobcoins, and Pro Plans on IBM i." *Nick Litten Blog*, n.d.
<https://www.nicklitten.com/ibm-bob-pricing-explained-free-trial-bobcoins-and-pro-plans-on-ibm-i/>
**Tier:** 3
Confirms Pro/Pro Plus/Ultra prices and Bobcoin counts in [26]. Bobcoin = ~$0.50 USD if exceeding monthly allowance. Usage examples: simple explanations 0.1-0.5 coins; full program modernization 2-5; documentation generation 1-3; CLI workflows 5-10 per run.

**[30]** Quach, Katyanna. "IBM's AI Bob could be manipulated to download and execute malware." *The Register*, January 7, 2026.
<https://www.theregister.com/2026/01/07/ibm_bob_vulnerability/>
**Tier:** 2
PromptArmor research disclosed three flaws in IBM Bob (then in tech preview): (1) process substitution bypass — Bob blocks `$(command)` but not process substitution; (2) command chaining via `>` redirection allowing malicious instructions to follow approved echo commands; (3) markdown image rendering with permissive CSP enables zero-click data exfiltration via pre-fetched JSON schemas. Attack scenario: malicious README.md in a code repo. IBM said it had "no record" of direct notification, emphasized tech-preview status, and committed to remediation before GA. **Patch status at March 24, 2026 GA is not confirmed in the Register coverage.**

## Cross-cutting benchmarks and counter-perspectives

**[31]** "SWE-bench leaderboards." *swebench.com*, accessed April 26, 2026.
<https://www.swebench.com/>
**Tier:** 1
Official Princeton/CMU benchmark. Variants: Verified, Multilingual, Lite, Full, Multimodal. Specific top entries not extractable from a single fetch; see [32] for aggregator.

**[32]** "SWE-bench Verified leaderboard tracker." *BenchLM*, April 2026.
<https://benchlm.ai/benchmarks/sweVerified>
**Tier:** 3
Aggregated SWE-bench Verified scores: Claude Mythos Preview 93.9% (preview/unconfirmed model name); Claude Opus 4.7 (Adaptive) 87.6%; GPT-5.3 Codex 85%; Claude Opus 4.6 80.8%; Claude Sonnet 4.6 79.6%; GPT-5.2 80.0%; Gemini 2.5 Pro 63.8%. Gemini 3 Pro/Flash and IBM Granite NOT listed.

**[33]** "SWE-bench Pro: Why scores collapsed and what it actually measures." *MorphLLM*, n.d.
<https://www.morphllm.com/swe-bench-pro>
**Tier:** 3
SEAL standardized scaffolding (250-turn limit), enterprise-grade tasks. Top SEAL scores: Claude Opus 4.5 45.9%, Sonnet 4.5 43.6%, Gemini 3 Pro 43.3%. Verified-vs-Pro gap on Opus 4.5: 80.9% → 45.9% (~35-point spread). Pro tasks modify "an average of 4.1 files" with "107.4 lines changed" (vs single-file Verified tasks). Same model varies 50.2-55.4% on Pro depending on agent framework.

**[34]** Becker, Joel et al. "Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity." *METR*, July 10, 2025. Also arXiv:2507.09089.
<https://metr.org/blog/2025-07-10-early-2025-ai-experienced-os-dev-study/>
**Tier:** 1
Randomized controlled trial: 16 experienced open-source developers, 246 real GitHub issues, ~2 hours each. Result: developers using AI tools took **19% longer** to complete issues. Developers expected AI to speed them up 24%; even after experiencing the slowdown, they believed AI sped them up 20%. Tools used: Cursor Pro with Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet (frontier at the time). Compensation $150/hour; screen recordings used for verification. Confidence intervals "forthcoming" in appendices.

**[35]** "AI Copilot Code Quality: 2025 Look at Code Patterns." *GitClear*, 2025.
<https://www.gitclear.com/ai_assistant_code_quality_2025_research>
**Tier:** 2
211 million changed lines analyzed, January 2020 — December 2024, repos owned by Google, Microsoft, Meta, and enterprise C-Corps. Code duplication rose from 8.3% to 12.3% of changed lines (~48% increase). Refactoring rate fell from 25% (2021) to under 10% (2024). "Copy/pasted code exceeded moved code for the first time in history." Claim of "4× more code cloning" appears as a separate framing in the report.

**[36]** "When Coding Agents Spiral Into 693 Lines of Hallucinations." *Surge HQ Blog*, February 5, 2026.
<https://surgehq.ai/blog/when-coding-agents-spiral-into-693-lines-of-hallucinations>
**Tier:** 3
Real SWE-bench task: astropy HTML writer `formats` argument bug (2-line fix). Three frontier models tested:
- **Gemini 2.5 Pro:** 39 turns, 693 modified lines, never solved. Fabricated `core.BaseWriter` class, invented `get_col_str_iters()` method, hallucinated terminal output and line numbers.
- **Claude Sonnet 4:** Made errors but recovered after encountering reality, ultimately solved.
- **GPT-5:** Flagged truncation gaps, re-inspected, solved cleanly first attempt.

**[37]** Orosz, Gergely and Wienberg, Elin. "AI Tooling for Software Engineers in 2026." *The Pragmatic Engineer*, February-March 2026.

Findings: 95% use AI weekly+; 75% use AI for ≥50% of work; 56% do 70%+ work with AI; 55% regularly use agents; 70% juggle 2-4 tools simultaneously; 46% identify Claude Code as their most-loved tool. Tool ranking by mentions: 1) Claude Code, 2) Chatbots, 3) GitHub Copilot, 4) Cursor, 5) Codex. Authors note: "self-selected, relatively experienced audience rather than a random sample."
